discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moiré quantum materials)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that electron interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally. Through careful tear-and-stack fabrication and low-temperature transport, they found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. These results created twistronics: the twist angle became a new control parameter, and a single tunable, gate-controlled device could show strongly correlated phases such as superconductivity, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators and, in moiré TMDs, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states. The prediction was simple and its experimental confirmation rigorous. Laboratories around the world, including many outside the traditional centres, now study strongly correlated electrons in moiré van der Waals platforms, and this work has lastingly changed how condensed-matter physicists explore quantum matter.
